about: Falsifiable prediction written BEFORE the 1-agent real-trace replay of the GLM-5.3-Flash seat on snoopy (RTX 3090 Ti + RAM tier). It replaces the INFERRED ~20 tok/s GLM figure in the handoff with a matched measurement against R8's n1 run (32.6 useful tok/s). Do not edit the predicted numbers after the run; add a 'measured' block beside them.
recipe: snoopy GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 3.05 bpw seat (ledger row snoopy-glm-seat-trim-c-64k: route trim keep 4 on layers 29-44, 107 GiB RAM tier, batch 1), served by serve.py over exllamav3; replay: agent-replay.py run --trace agent-long-16 --agents 1 --warmup-s 300 --duration-s 600 --stagger-scale 0.02 (same args as R8's n1 run, results/night/1026T1608).
equation: per turn: t = out/D + fresh/P + gap; useful = out/t. out and fresh per turn and the gap are taken from R8's n1 run on the same trace (72 turns, 19,574 out, 158,383 fresh, so F 8.09; tool gaps ~22 % of R8's 600 s = 1.83 s a turn). The model generates its own lengths, so out per turn may differ.

D.src: row snoopy-glm-seat-trim-c-64k, C1 decode short prompts (25.6-26.7 at 16k)

gap_s_per_turn.src: 22 % of R8 n1's window over 72 turns

falsifies: useful outside 14-22, or decode median outside 22-28, says the per-turn model or the seat's measured D/P does not hold on real agent prompts (for example no prefix reuse in the server, which would raise fresh tokens per turn several-fold).

measured.src: lab notes (agent-replay, 1 agent, 300 s warm-up, 600 s window, 0 errors)

turns_per_agent_min.verdict: the predicted 1.82 ratio holds on turns, not on tokens

decode_tok_s_median.verdict: UNREADABLE: serve.py sends a turn's output in one chunk at the end (dur == ttft on most turns), so client timing cannot split decode from prefill

why_it_missed: MEASURED: GLM wrote 76 tokens a turn (median) where R8 wrote 182 and the recording 298; useful tok/s scales with that, so it is the wrong yardstick across models; turns per agent-minute is the matched one.
MEASURED: a turn took 11.4 s against a predicted ~5.8 s for 76 tokens (76/25.9 + 2200/761).

INFERRED: the extra ~5.5 s is prompt re-reading; at 761 tok/s that is ~6.5k fresh tokens a turn against R8's 915 median, so the seat's exllamav3 prefix reuse keeps much less of a 55k agent prompt than strata's conversation cache. Not measured: the server reports no cached_tokens.
measured.lesson: Compare models on turns per agent-minute (or tasks per hour), not useful tok/s; and the per-turn model needs each server's measured prefix reuse, not R8's fresh-token count.

rescore_turn_model.about: Re-score with the per-turn agent model (src/model.js agentReplaySim; data/workload.json turn_model), added after the measurements; the predictions above stay as written. before = this file's own numbers (turns derived where the old model gave only useful tok/s: its useful / the run's measured output a turn); after = the model with every input; held_out = the same with the inputs measured on the scored run replaced by what existed without it (each input's held_out value, else the fallbacks turn_model states). after_at_commit = the model's numbers when this block was written (tests/test_workload.js checks they still hold). node report.js --accuracy prints the table
rescore_turn_model.model: src/model.js agentTurnPredict (fluid replay of the trace: turn = out / D1 + fresh / P alone, then the recorded tool gap; shared server w = out / Dn + fresh / P)

stall.src: serve.py at batch 1: a turn's read and its decode run in turn
